lede: Raising β blurs the digit and turns unused latent axes off. Diversity peaks at β = 1, not at the Optuna pick.
title: β-VAE on digits
question: What does the KL weight do to reconstruction, active latent axes, and sample diversity?
process: The loss is per-image squared error plus β times the closed-form KL. Latent width is fixed at 8. The sweep fits β in {0.1, 1, 4, 10} for 10 epochs from the same initialization, on 1,000 training images and 200 test images of each class. An active unit is a latent axis whose posterior mean still varies across the test set (variance above 0.01). Diversity is the mean pairwise per-pixel squared distance of 64 prior samples. A traversal walks one coordinate of the zero code from −3 to 3. Optuna minimizes the β-weighted validation loss and selects β = 0.1 (val loss 100.37). The directory name is mnist_betta_vae.

opening.summary: The three panels move together. Reconstruction MSE rises with β, active axes fall from 8 to 6, and diversity peaks at β = 1. Hover a β to swap the traversal grid.

charts.title: Test MSE, active axes, and diversity

marks.summary: β = 0.1 has the sharpest reconstructions in the sweep (test MSE 0.0907) and all 8 axes stay active. Per-axis KL sits in a narrow band, about 3.1 to 3.8. Every traversal row changes the digit. Diversity is 0.168, tighter than β = 1. Optuna picks this β because it minimizes the weighted loss, which is the best reconstruction here and not the most compact code.
marks.frameCaption: Latent traversal at β = 0.1. Every row changes the digit.

marks.summary: β = 1 is the standard VAE in this sweep. Test MSE rises only to 0.0940, all 8 axes stay active, and diversity peaks at 0.226. KL falls to 15.03. The rows still change the glyph. This is the best generation diversity, not the point Optuna selected.
marks.frameCaption: Latent traversal at β = 1, the diversity peak.

marks.answers: Why do you think the results might not be great?
marks.summary: β = 4 pushes test MSE to 0.1114 and KL down to 8.37. Active units fall to 7. One axis, z4, has KL about 0.007 and a traversal response near zero. Diversity slips to 0.204. The code is getting smaller by switching an axis off, and the digits are blurrier.
marks.frameCaption: Latent traversal at β = 4. One axis has nearly stopped moving.

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: β = 10 is the blurriest decoder (test MSE 0.1480) and the least diverse prior (0.151). KL is 3.94. z3, z4, and z5 each have KL under 0.02 and their traversal rows barely move: three rows of the grid stay a single glyph. The rows that still move still change which digit you see. That is unused axes turning off, not one axis owning slant. MNIST does not label a continuous factor, so the grid is not a disentanglement claim.
marks.frameCaption: Latent traversal at β = 10. Three rows stay frozen.

reflection.worked: The sweep separates the three effects the bonus asks for. Small β reconstructs. β = 1 is the most diverse. Large β turns axes off, and the traversal pictures show which rows died.
reflection.unexpected: The search does not pick the diverse or the compact model. It picks β = 0.1, because that is the smallest weighted loss. High β does not reveal a single factor such as slant; the dead rows are unused capacity.
reflection.why: β multiplies the KL, so a large weight is cheaper to satisfy by pinning posterior means than by preserving stroke detail. Diversity falls at both ends: β = 0.1 concentrates the prior samples, and β = 10 has directions that no longer change the image. The active-unit count is a variance threshold, not a labeled-factor score.
reflection.improve: Report reconstruction and diversity beside the Optuna objective, or the search will always prefer a small β. For a real disentanglement check, use a dataset with known factors. On MNIST, keep β near 1 if the goal is the sample grid, and use the traversal only to see which axes went quiet.
